description: We are Velocity Labs, an international team building ASTRAL Crew for the astronaut health-monitoring challenge. Khalid develops wearable analysis, Benjamin voice analysis, Aarika the backend, Eleni NASA research and data, and Anuj the interface. Together we turn synthetic crew signals and NASA research into a clear, human-reviewed health dashboard. We bring software, data, design and space-health interests to the project.
summary: ASTRAL Crew is an offline-first astronaut health-monitoring prototype for long-duration missions. It brings an astronaut's self-reported and measured health indicators together with a personal baseline, makes unusual multi-indicator patterns easier to review, and links the astronaut to clear next steps and mission hazard context. Its prototype uses synthetic daily telemetry and a transparent rolling-median / median-absolute-deviation (MAD) comparison; it does not diagnose, predict disease, or control spacecraft systems.
details: ASTRAL Crew helps astronauts review health changes when communication with Earth is delayed. Our five-member synthetic mission demo combines vital signs, voice and wrist signals, and cabin conditions. It shows personal trends, missing or invalid readings, and findings for human review. NASA's five human-spaceflight hazards provide context; a separate Biology Evidence view plots real NASA OSDR OSD-575 serum data from Inspiration4, clearly apart from the simulated crew. We built the prototype with Python, NumPy/SciPy, SQLite, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, plus an exploratory WESAD-based wearable model. Its creative focus is comparing individual signals with shared cabin changes without claiming a cause. It runs locally without a cloud service. The demo is educational: it does not diagnose stress, provide flight-approved treatment, or control spacecraft systems. AI assistants helped with research, writing, coding and debugging; our team chose the concept, reviewed sources and integrated the work.
